title: NYC's Own Chapter Gallery, and the Communities Scope Boundary in Writing
userRequest: Project context: We need to modernize the https://www.harvardintech.com/ website from the outside. The site was built with a no-code product so we need to faithfully reproduce it using modern technologies and host it as a GitHub pages website. It also needs a CRM that can be run locally or, ideally also in the cloud via GitHub pages as well (protected with a password and/or GitHub OAuth). Can we dig into this?
description: Closes the two steps the per-chapter photo galleries plan left unimplemented. `src/content/chapters/nyc.md` now carries a `photos` list of 14 images, so /chapters/nyc renders its own gallery under a 'Photos from New York City' heading instead of the shared 40-photo event wall — five columns, twelve shown, the remaining two behind a 'Show all 14 photos' control that reflows the set into one continuous 5/5/4 grid. The photos are deliberately uncaptioned: the repo holds no NYC-specific photography and no true caption facts, so the committed entry asserts nothing it cannot support, and Nicole adds real captions from /admin where the lightbox already renders them. `src/pages/communities/[slug].astro` gained a frontmatter comment recording that `photos` is never passed on purpose — the boundary is enforced twice over, since the communities schema declares no such field — placed in frontmatter rather than markup so it stays out of the served HTML. A new guard, `src/lib/chapter.photos.test.ts`, holds every chapter's declared photo paths to being non-blank, root-absolute (a relative path would resolve against the route once `withBase` runs) and present under public/; it was verified red by typo'ing a path, and it deliberately does not assert that any chapter declares photos at all, since clearing a gallery from the CMS is an ordinary editorial act rather than a CI failure. Two things surfaced worth carrying forward: a content-only edit is invisible to the screenshot freshness math, which tracks source imports rather than content collections, so /chapters/nyc's capture had to be forced; and the dev server reads content from a sandbox snapshot that wins over src/content, which silently masked the change through two restarts.
